documents.path: WWW / Blog / Why MCP Is Awesome

values.value: The Model Context Protocol turns your CMS from a black box into a toolbox. Here is why that changes everything.

value.markup:
What MCP actually is

MCP — the Model Context Protocol — is an open standard for connecting AI agents to the systems they work with. Think of it as USB-C for AI: one plug, many devices. An agent that speaks MCP can discover what a server offers, call those capabilities with structured inputs, and get structured results back.

Umbraco ships an MCP server that exposes the CMS's own management API as tools: read the content tree, create document types, publish pages, upload media. No screen-scraping, no custom integrations — the agent uses the same API a backoffice user would.

values.value: A screen full of colourful source code — photo by Chris Ried on Unsplash.
An API you can call is worth a thousand prompts you have to babysit.

value.markup:
Why that is awesome

  • Tools, not prompts. The agent calls real API operations — create, update, publish — instead of hoping a prompt produces the right JSON.
  • Schema first. Every tool has a typed input and output, so results are predictable and errors are loud.
  • Least privilege. The MCP server authenticates with its own API user and scopes what an agent may do.
  • Composable. The same server works from any MCP client — CLI agents, IDEs, chat apps.

That is the whole trick: the CMS stops being a black box and becomes a toolbox the agent can actually use.

values.value: Why MCP Is Awesome for Editors
MCP meets editors where they already work: the backoffice stays the source of truth, and the agent does the typing.

value.markup:
If you spend your days in the Umbraco backoffice, MCP is awesome for a very concrete reason: it meets you where you already work. The agent is just another client of the same management API — it creates the draft, sets the properties, adds the blocks, and asks you to hit publish.

You keep the editorial controls. The agent gets the typing.

values.value: The model proposes, the CMS disposes — in the best possible way.
Two hands fitting puzzle pieces together — photo by Vardan Papikyan on Unsplash.

value.markup:
Where this is going

Every block on this page was placed by an agent through the Umbraco MCP server: the schema, the content, the media, the publish. The Razor views rendering it were written the same afternoon. That is the whole pitch — an open protocol, an honest API, and a CMS that was built to be extended.

Go make something awesome.
